acceptance: The help text and any other user-facing description of allow_insecure_gateway state that it turns off OCSP revocation checking only, and that certificate verification still applies
Or, if accepting self-signed gateways is the intended behaviour, the option implements it and a test proves a self-signed endpoint is accepted only with the option set
The site page docs/platforms/snowflake-gateways.md stays consistent with the result
context: Found by an independent review of the site page docs/platforms/snowflake-gateways.md against core v0.5.1 (91d357a); each claim was re-verified by a second reviewer.
description: core/gateway.py:222 describes allow_insecure_gateway as 'Allow insecure (TLS disabled / self-signed) gateway connection'. The option only sets the Snowflake connector's insecure_mode (platforms/snowflake.py:684-685), which turns off OCSP revocation checks. Certificate and host name verification still run, so a self-signed or untrusted gateway still fails TLS. From connector 4.8.0, insecure_mode also turns OCSP off when gateway_ocsp_fail_open is set, so the two options interact.
